- **Trust decision:** the `--studio` server accepted requests from anyone (it listened on every network interface, allowed any web origin and had no login). It passed the request's `agent` and `prompt` into processes started through a shell. The fix changes six places, all in `cli-tool/src/sandbox-server.js`.
- **`pattern_fit`:** B.
- **Strongest lever:** the fix's agent-name check in `cli-tool/src/sandbox-server.js:271-275` runs only after an early "agent already exists" return. A name whose path collapses (through `../`) onto an existing `.md` file skips the check. It then reaches a shell command in the cloud-mode Python launcher (`cli-tool/components/sandbox/e2b/e2b-launcher.py:151-152`). That is in another language and directory and runs in a "secure cloud sandbox", which gives a solver an easy reason to dismiss it. I worked this out from the code and did not run it, so it is listed under `unverified`.
- **Biggest red flag:** none of the defined flags apply. Risks: all six fix sites are in one file, the bypass is unconfirmed, the uncovered shell runs in the remote cloud sandbox rather than on the user's machine, and there is no latest tree to check whether it is still present.
